title: Sticky canary and hidden promotion due to routing policy merge conflict
creator: Lina Chen
description: During a scheduled canary rollout of model v2026-03-05 (text-gen-3b), an unexpected partial promotion occurred: ~15% of production traffic was served by the canary for multiple hours beyond the intended canary window. The console and API both reported the rollout as 0->10%->50% in the control plane, but dataplane routing applied a transient additional weight resulting in sticky canary sessions. This ticket tracks the follow-up investigation, interim mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-08 09:12 UTC — Canary rollout initiated (10% target) via console - rollout-id rlt-20260308-117
2026-03-08 09:14 UTC — Concurrent automation job (autopromote) evaluated metrics for previous rollout and issued a separate routing-policy update for a different service (svc-payments).
2026-03-08 09:15–09:17 UTC — Control plane accepted both updates; merge order resulted in a combined routing configuration containing both route fragments. No validation error thrown.

2026-03-08 09:18 UTC — Dataplane observed a policy fragment collision and applied a conservative union behavior for traffic weights, effectively increasing canary weight to ~25% for sessions originating during 09:18–10:50 UTC.
2026-03-08 09:45 UTC — Customer SRE alerted on anomalous latency/throughput in a downstream service; investigation correlated to increased canary traffic.
2026-03-08 10:52 UTC — Manual rollback to 0% canary performed; dataplane restored to expected weights by 11:00 UTC.
2026-03-08 11:30 UTC — Post-rollback monitoring verified stable traffic split and normal latencies.
impact: Medium. ~15% unexpected exposure to canary model for ~1.5 hours. No data exfiltration or customer-visible errors recorded, but increased latencies and cost. A small subset of user sessions saw model outputs from the canary variant causing inconsistency in results for end-users and A/B analysis noise for product telemetry.
root_cause: A merge-time race between two independent routing-policy updates (console-triggered rollout fragment and an automation autopromote fragment) produced a combined policy that the dataplane interpreted permissively. The routing policy merge algorithm currently applies a union of overlapping route fragments and additive weight semantics when fragments conflict; this behavior was neither documented nor guarded by validation. Additionally, there was no canonical source-of-truth enforcement for rollout ownership and no pre-apply dry-run that would have flagged the surprising merged semantics.
mitigation: Immediate: Manual rollback and targeted drain of affected sessions (completed 2026-03-08).
Short-term: Added a control-plane guard to reject concurrent overlapping routing updates for the same logical route unless explicitly marked as additive (hotfix deployed 2026-03-09).
Monitoring: Dashboards updated to surface percent-of-sessions-by-model and session-origin timestamps to detect sticky-session exposure earlier.
action_items: Add atomic merge semantics for routing policy updates: treat overlapping fragments as replace-with-consensus rather than union (design doc + spec) — due 2026-04-02.
Implement pre-apply dry-run validation that simulates merged policy on a staging dataplane and emits a diff with explicit warnings for additive weight effects — owner: Marco Rivera — due 2026-03-27.
Introduce rollout ownership metadata and a soft-lock for routes to prevent independent autopromote jobs from modifying the same route concurrently — owner: Priya Nambiar — due 2026-03-21.
E2E test: Add integration test that exercises concurrent routing updates and asserts deterministic final weights across the control and data planes — owner: QA Team (Sven Ho) — due 2026-03-31.
Operational: Create a ‘kill-switch’ emergency route that immediately pins traffic to a known-good variant for a given tenant — owner: Oncall Tools — due 2026-03-20.
Documentation: Update routing policy docs to explicitly describe merge semantics and corner cases; include example conflict scenarios — owner: Docs (Aisha Patel) — due 2026-03-18.
Post-incident review: Run a tabletop on 2026-03-16 with Console/Autoscale/Dataplane teams to walk through the race and validate runbook updates — owner: Lina Chen — scheduled 2026-03-16.
